question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2}$ of two balls is drawn from a population. The population has balls of two different weights, $75\,\text{g}$ and $\text{90}\,\text{g},$ distributed in the ratio $4:2.$ Calculate $\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}].$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sequence of random variables representing a random sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with population mean $\mu .$ Then, the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is given by

$$
\overset{―}{X}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{X}_{i}.
$$

Since $\overset{―}{X}$ is an unbiased estimator of $\mu ,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu .
$$

We're told that the balls in the population weigh $75\,\text{g}$ and $\text{90}\,\text{g},$ and these are distributed in the ratio $4:2.$ Therefore, to compute the population mean, we can consider a population consisting of $4+2=6$ balls only with the following weights:

$$
75\,\text{g},\,75\,\text{g},\,75\,\text{g},\,75\,\text{g},\,90\,\text{g},\,90\,\text{g}.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{6}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(4\cdot 75+2\cdot 90) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(300+180) \\  & =\frac{480}{6} \\  & =80\,\text{g}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu =80\,\text{g}.
$$
